reviews.one_line_contribution: That a ~300-token object→receptacle frequency table compiled by rule from an ALFWorld expert pool — a cross-episode aggregate that k retrieved trajectories cannot contain — recovers the retrieval gain on search-bound task types at zero uncached prefill, with the gain attributed to aggregation (depth-at-fixed-coverage ladder), to content (row-deranged placebo), to experience (no-bank LLM-written table), and to explicitness (whole 80-item bank in context with and without its own table).
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three verified works, none cited by the proposal, are the real threat, and the omission is itself a novelty problem. (1) ExpeL, arXiv:2308.10144 (verified, HF) — extracts cross-trajectory natural-language insights from an experience pool and evaluates them on ALFWorld together with retrieved successful trajectories, ablating insights against retrieval-only; that ablation is structurally the proposal's 'static3 + cheatsheet vs k3' and 'whole-bank ± its own table' contrast, just with LLM-written rules instead of a rule-compiled frequency count, and without token matching, depth variation, or a placebo. (2) AutoGuide, arXiv:2403.08978 (verified, S2, NeurIPS 2024, 65 cites) — compiles state-conditioned guidelines from offline experience and beats in-context-example baselines, i.e. compiled-from-experience artifact vs raw demonstrations already exists as a comparison. (3) AutoManual, arXiv:2405.16247 (verified, HF) — builds rule manuals from ALFWorld interaction. Against these, what survives as new is narrow but real: none compiles a *statistic* (a count over the whole pool) rather than rules/procedures, none matches tokens or accounts for prefix caching, and none runs a coverage-matched depth ladder or a token-matched deranged placebo to attribute the gain. The nearest domain-specific work, 'Zero-Shot Embodied Decision Making with Structured Prior Knowledge and Adaptive Calibration in ALFWorld' (WCCIS 2026, verified on S2, no arXiv id), already shows hand-built object-location priors drive ALFWorld search for a symbolic controller — it does not compile from experience or compare with an LLM reader's retrieval, so it motivates rather than pre-empts, but it does mean the mechanism's existence is not the contribution.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline is tested against a retriever chosen so it cannot win. k=3 goal-sentence retrieval returns three whole trajectories selected by task type; nothing in the plan runs the retrieval arm that could actually carry placement information — object-class-conditioned retrieval (retrieve k trajectories that contain the target object) or k enlarged within the object class. With ~30 object classes over 1,465 trajectories such a retriever returns k independent placement samples for exactly the object the agent must find, i.e. the d=k rung of the proposal's own ladder plus the instance binding. So 'retrieval structurally cannot carry a cross-episode aggregate' is only tested as 'this type-keyed retriever does not,' and the general form is close to definitional (three sampled trajectories obviously do not contain a 1,465-item count). Second, the plausible branch of P4 destroys the contribution: the proposal itself expects ALFWorld placements to be stereotyped, and if the no-bank LLM-written table matches the compiled one, the result reduces to 'tell the model where household objects usually live,' already established by the verified WCCIS 2026 ALFWorld agent and by the robotics placement-prior line. Between a stronger retriever above and commonsense below, the band in which the claim is both true and interesting is thin, and neither boundary is instrumented.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Add object-class-conditioned retrieval (k=3 and k=7 restricted to trajectories containing the target object, token-matched) as the retrieval arm P1 and P5 are scored against, and report the compiled table's advantage over *that*; this is the arm that turns a near-tautology into a measurement of how many samples of aggregation retrieval can buy per token. Add an LLM-compiled-from-bank table (ExpeL/Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style compiler on the same 1,465 items) so 'compilation' means what the literature means by it, not only a hand-specified extraction rule. Pad cheatsheet_d1 to ~300 tokens in the same format so P2 is not depth-versus-length. Make P7's primary scoring the succeeded-in-both stratum — as written, ceiling-scoring no-take episodes converts P1's success gain mechanically into the receptacle reduction. Give P8 a branch that stops the run (a paired equivalence band from re-run noise, ≈±6, not the ±12 cell floor, and a stated k3−k0 outcome that aborts rather than only rescaling M1) — a gate whose every branch is 'proceed' is not a gate. Score P3 as an equivalence of shuffled_all to k0 (or set its margin at M1 plus the measured shuffled−k0 gap) so it can fail independently of P1. Finally, cite and position against ExpeL/AutoGuide/AutoManual, and pre-register what is claimed if P4 nulls.
reviews.missing_baseline: Object-class-conditioned retrieval — k trajectories retrieved because they contain the target object class (and the same at larger k), token-matched and cached-cost-accounted. It is the only retrieval arm that can carry placement statistics, and its absence means the central 'what retrieval cannot carry' claim is measured against a type-keyed retriever rather than against retrieval. Secondary omission: an LLM-compiled table built from the bank (as opposed to the no-bank LLM-prior), which is what every compiled-memory system in the literature actually does.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision, and the proposal's own check is genuine but incomplete in the one direction that matters. Queries I ran, all answered by channel (a) the s2cli command (S2 + HF; WebSearch is unavailable in this session, so no query used channel (b)): Q1 'compiled object-location statistics from agent trajectories versus retrieval in LLM agents' --recent → nothing on the claim (nearest: 2606.19911 Multi-Agent Transactive Memory, 2604.04949 Learning to Retrieve from Agent Trajectories). Q2 'aggregate statistics cheatsheet static prompt beats per-query retrieval agent memory ALFWorld' --recent → nothing on the claim (2605.05413 constant-context skill learning, 2605.16986 test-time skill synthesis, 2608.14943 skill-loading caching comparison). Q3 'cross-episode aggregated knowledge summary outperforms retrieved exemplars matched token budget agent' --recent → empty of relevant hits. Q4 'insights extracted across trajectories added to retrieved demonstrations ablation embodied agent guidelines' --recent → empty of relevant hits. Q5 (closest named method) 'Dynamic Cheatsheet test-time learning persistent memory reusable strategies' → 2504.07952 not returned by the query but verified directly; nearest new work 2606.05684 AdaMEM, 2512.10696 ReMe, 2509.04439 ArcMemo — none compares a compiled artifact with retrieval of the raw episodes at matched tokens. Q6 (home literature, no agent/memory words) 'object receptacle co-occurrence frequency prior for household object search embodied agent' → 2607.00022 PerSim (verified), 2305.17537 Scene Graph Memory, 2207.10761 TIDEE, 2108.00159 — the mechanism is established outside agent memory, as the proposal says. Q7 'ExpeL … experience pool ALFWorld' and Q8 'AutoGuide state-aware guidelines' → surfaced the works the proposal does not cite (2308.10144, 2403.08978, 2405.16247, 2606.27136 JERP). Q9 'long-context models fail at aggregation over many documents' → 2410.11996 HoloBench, 2407.00402 — P6's 'the reader is not an aggregator' is already the expected answer in the long-context QA literature, so it is a confirmation, not a discovery. Q10 verified the WCCIS 2026 ALFWorld prior-knowledge paper on S2 (real, no arXiv id, 2026-07-01), as the proposal states. ID verification: VERIFIED — 2504.07952 (Dynamic Cheatsheet), 2511.07800 (strategy/graph memory), 2606.03951 (Demo2Tutorial), 2406.14596 (ICAL), 2605.24117 (SkillEvolBench), 2607.00022 (PerSim), 2308.10144, 2403.08978, 2405.16247. COULD NOT VERIFY on S2 or HF — 2512.23760 (cited as verifier-promoted skill graphs) and 2603.05642 ('SymSearch', cited as robotics evidence that the placement-prior mechanism exists); both are load-bearing for the related-work framing and one of them for the home-literature argument, and the authors should re-check the ids. Judgement of the check itself: three queries with named ids and one genuine no-agent-words home query is above average for this round, but it searched the location-prior literature and the cheatsheet literature and never the compiled-rules-from-experience literature (ExpeL, AutoGuide, AutoManual) where the closest work actually sits — so the check's 'no pre-emption' verdict is not established for the compilation half of the claim.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That a ~300-token rule-compiled table of object-to-receptacle placement frequencies, aggregated across the whole expert pool and served as a cached type-agnostic static prefix, carries cross-episode information that top-k retrieved trajectories structurally cannot, and that on ALFWorld's search-bound task types it matches the retrieval gain over no memory at zero uncached prefill and erases the residual that k=3 retains over the best static arm - with derangement, depth-at-fixed-coverage, a no-experience LLM-written table, and a whole-bank-with-and-without-its-own-table pair used to attribute the gain to aggregation rather than to scaffold, coverage, pretraining, or implicit extraction by the reader.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, of different kinds. (1) Closest named method: Dynamic Cheatsheet, arXiv:2504.07952 (verified via s2cli, S2 record: EACL, 113 citations) - a persistent evolving cheatsheet of reusable insights written at test time. It does not threaten the specific claim: its artifact is insight text, not a cross-episode frequency statistic; it never runs a retrieval-of-raw-episodes arm at matched tokens, and it never varies how much experience is compiled. The proposal's characterization of it is accurate. (2) The real threat is to the mechanism, not to the comparison: the embodied/robotics line already establishes that object-receptacle placement statistics drive object search. Verified: arXiv:2607.00022 (PerSim, 'When to Personalize Household Object Search', 2026-06-18, S2, 2 cit) trains room-level priors and within-room co-occurrence cues for household object search; arXiv:2207.10761 (TIDEE) and arXiv:2305.17537 (Scene Graph Memory, object-location prediction in partially observable homes) predate it, and arXiv:2607.14514 (VTM-Nav, 2026-07-16, hf) reuses cross-episode experience for object-goal navigation. Adjacent and worth citing: arXiv:2308.00675 (Tool Documentation Enables Zero-Shot Tool-Usage) already shows a compiled description substituting for demonstrations - the general 'compiled artifact beats retrieved examples' move is not new, only its instantiation as a frequency table against a trajectory retriever is. Against that background, the contribution reduces to the attribution structure (derangement, depth-at-fixed-coverage, LLM-prior, whole-bank pair) rather than the finding that placement statistics help. The proposal's named WCCIS 2026 symbolic-agent paper ('Zero-Shot Embodied Decision Making with Structured Prior Knowledge') is the nearest overlap it identifies, but it has no arXiv id and I could not verify it through the available channel; treat it as unverified.
reviews.strongest_objection: The most probable single outcome hollows out the headline. The proposal itself concedes in Limitations that ALFWorld placements are sampled from generic plausibility and are scene-agnostic - which is exactly the condition under which the LLM-prior arm (P4) matches the compiled table. P4 demands that experience beat Qwen3-32B's own same-format, same-vocabulary table by M2 = +7 points on ~30 stereotyped object classes; that is a large ask, and if it fails, 'cross-episode statistics compiled from the bank' collapses to 'write the commonsense placement prior into the prompt', which is a prompt-engineering observation the robotics line (2607.00022, 2207.10761, 2305.17537) and the proposal's own WCCIS reference already assume. The title claim, and the brief's compilation-from-experience framing, would be unsupported by the experiment that was run. A second, compounding objection: the headline P1 is scored against k0, not against static3, even though the round's binding rule makes the best static arm the baseline. cheatsheet_all - static3 is 'reported' but carries no pre-registered margin and no falsifier, so the study cannot fail on the comparison the round exists to force. Third, the entailment check's two near-entailments are acknowledged and then not fixed: with shuffled_all at or below k0, P1 at M1 algebraically delivers P3 at M1, and P7's ceiling scoring of no-take episodes converts P1's success gain directly into the receptacle-count reduction - so of eight predictions, two are re-expressions of the headline, and P8 is a gate whose every branch proceeds with an acceptance band set equal to the noise floor.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Make P4 the headline, not an attribution ablation. The claim worth an ICLR slot is 'compiled experience beats the model's own prior', so cheatsheet_all - LLM_prior should be P1 with the margin, and cheatsheet_all - k0 demoted to a manipulation check; alternatively, plant the divergence - perturb the ALFWorld placement distribution (regenerate or filter games so a subset of object classes sits at non-modal receptacles) and build the bank from the perturbed distribution, giving two levels of prior-experience divergence and turning a named property into a manipulated one. That single change also satisfies the round's 'manipulate, do not observe' rule, which the current design meets only for the artifact, not for the environment property. (2) Attach a pre-registered margin and falsifier to cheatsheet_all - static3 and to the type-agnostic combo instr_all + cheatsheet_all, and run the latter at 8 seeds rather than at 2 seeds with a +/-12 floor - it, not the static3 combo, is the rule-compliant test of P5. (3) Adopt the entailment check's fixes verbatim: set P3's margin at M1 plus the measured shuffled_all - k0 gap (or score it as equivalence of shuffled_all to k0), make P7's both-arms-take restricted version primary, and give P8 a paired-equivalence band from re-run noise plus at least one k3 - k0 branch that stops the run. (4) Add the two arms named under missing_baseline.
reviews.missing_baseline: An object-conditioned retriever: k=3 trajectories selected because they contain the target object class, token-matched to k3. The title asserts what retrieval cannot carry, but the plan only runs the goal-sentence retriever from Measurement A, which selects by task type and therefore rarely returns the target object's placements. A trivial string-match retriever over the same 1,465-item pool does deliver placement evidence per query, and it costs one extra arm on hardware that already holds the bank. Without it the claim is not 'retrieval structurally cannot aggregate' but 'this particular retriever does not retrieve placements', and a reviewer will make that substitution in one sentence. Second omission, smaller but load-bearing for the content-vs-scaffold claim: there is no neutral scaffold arm. shuffled_all is an actively misleading table, so cheatsheet_all - shuffled_all confounds 'the right content helps' with 'the wrong content hurts' (the proposal half-sees this and adds only a reading rule). A uniform table - same format, same object classes, every receptacle in the vocabulary listed with no counts or equal counts, token-matched - is the arm that isolates the scaffold. Also absent: the self pool, which the brief names as the on-policy counterpart and which would test whether the statistic survives compilation from the agent's own noisier successes.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. My searches, all through channel (a) the s2cli command (S2 + HF together); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used, so no query was answered by channel (b). Q1 'compiled cross-episode statistics prompt versus retrieval agent memory' --recent: 12 hits, nearest 2603.02473 (retrieval vs write strategy in agent memory), 2605.18421 EvoMemBench (long-context baselines beat specialized memory), 2602.02007 (retrieval by decoupling and aggregation - aggregation over retrieved units, not a compiled static prefix); none compiles a cross-episode statistic and compares it with retrieval. Q2 'object receptacle location frequency table compiled from trajectories ALFWorld LLM agent' (all-time): nothing relevant. Q3 (closest named method) 'Dynamic Cheatsheet test-time learning persistent memory reusable strategies': 2504.07952, plus 2606.05684 AdaMEM, 2512.10696 ReMe, 2509.04439 ArcMemo - all insight/skill memories, none with a raw-retrieval control at matched tokens. Q4 'aggregate statistics across episodes into a prompt instead of retrieving individual trajectories' --recent: 6 hits, nearest 2607.07504 (LLM-generated skills do not reliably beat direct task prompting across thousands of runs - a supporting prior, not a collision). Q5 (home literature, no agent/memory/retrieval words) 'semantic placement prior object goal search co-occurrence statistics household embodied': 2207.10761 TIDEE, 2305.17537 Scene Graph Memory, 2302.12915, 2108.00159, 2607.14514 VTM-Nav - the mechanism is well established outside LLM agent memory, which caps novelty even without a collision. Q6 'compiled playbook fixed prompt versus retrieved trajectories matched token budget agent memory baseline' --recent: 2608.15008, 2605.13880 Preping, 2608.05784 Activity Frames; none runs the matched-token contrast. Q7 'summarized dataset statistics in prompt versus many-shot demonstrations in-context learning aggregation': 2308.00675 (documentation substitutes for demonstrations) is the nearest general precedent for the compiled-beats-examples move. On the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round - three query classes, channels named, IDs given, one query in the home vocabulary without agent/memory words, and a verdict that concedes the mechanism exists in robotics. ID verification: I verified 2504.07952, 2605.24117, 2406.14596, 2511.07800, 2512.23760, 2606.03951 and 2607.00022 through s2cli (all resolve, titles match the proposal's descriptions; note 2406.14596's S2 title is the ICAL NeurIPS paper, as claimed). I could NOT verify 2603.05642, cited as 'SymSearch' and used in the novelty argument to establish that the mechanism exists in robotics - s2cli returns 'not found on S2 or HF'. The WCCIS 2026 paper, which the proposal itself calls its nearest overlap, has no arXiv id and is unverifiable through the available channel; since it is the single closest work by the authors' own account, its unverifiability is a real gap in the novelty case rather than a formality.

reviews.one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld's search-bound task types, a ~300-token rule-compiled object-to-receptacle frequency table (a cross-episode aggregate no set of k retrieved trajectories contains) placed as a cached static prefix matches or beats k=3 retrieval at zero uncached prefill, with a depth-at-fixed-coverage ladder, a token-matched deranged table, a no-experience LLM-written table, and a whole-bank-with-and-without-its-own-table pair attributing the gain to aggregation of experience rather than coverage, scaffold, or pretraining.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified (literature command, S2+HF): arXiv 2607.00022 PerSim, 'When to Personalize Household Object Search: A Rigidity-Gated Hybrid Policy' (2026-06-18) — it uses population-frequency object-placement priors as the baseline policy for household object search and asks when trait-conditioned priors add over them; the mechanism the proposal wants to demonstrate (aggregated placement frequencies drive search efficiency) is its premise, not its finding. It does not threaten the specific contrast here (its priors are learned for a robot search policy, not an in-context artifact for an LLM reader, and it has no retrieval-of-raw-episodes arm at matched tokens), but it does mean the mechanism is not the novelty. Same for verified 2603.05642 (SymSearch: LLM relational knowledge distilled offline into lightweight models for interactive object search) and, older, 2302.12915 (S^4, LLM semantic spatial distributions for object search) and 2207.10761 (TIDEE, visuo-semantic commonsense placement priors) — both retrieved by my home-vocabulary query. On the method side the closest is verified 2504.07952 Dynamic Cheatsheet (2025-04, EACL, 113 citations): a compiled, persistently accumulated in-context artifact from experience; it never contrasts the compiled artifact with retrieval of the raw episodes and never varies how much experience is compiled, which is exactly the gap this proposal fills, so it constrains novelty to the attribution design rather than to the artifact. Net: what is new here is the placebo-controlled attribution of a compiled artifact's gain against a retrieval baseline at matched tokens, not the artifact or the mechanism.
reviews.strongest_objection: The study is scoped to the cell where the claim is cheapest, and the one contrast that carries the title's weight is one the authors themselves expect to come out null. (a) Cell S is precisely where Measurement A found retrieval weakest — look-at-in-light is -4.8 (retrieval hurts), pick types +15/+18, versus +39..+55 on clean/heat/cool — so M1=+10 is a pooled target that averages in a negative component, and the +20..+27 procedure-bound residual, which is the bulk of what retrieval actually buys on this node, is declared out of scope up front. 'What retrieval cannot carry' therefore turns out to be a small slice of what retrieval does carry. (b) P4 (cheatsheet_all - LLM-prior >= +7) is the load-bearing test of 'compiled from the bank', and the proposal concedes the null is plausible because ALFWorld placements are stereotyped; if a Qwen3-32B-authored table in the same format matches the compiled one, the paper's title claim is false and the result collapses to 'put an object-location table in the prompt', which robotics established years ago (2207.10761, 2302.12915) and which 2607.00022 uses as a baseline. (c) The automated entailment check is right that P3 and P7 are near-entailed by P1 and that P8's drift gate cannot fail (its band equals the 268-cell floor, and all three k3-k0 branches end in 'proceed'), so of eight predictions only P2, P4, P6 and the P5 additivity question carry independent information — on one environment and one backbone. An AC will ask what the paper says if P4 is null, and the honest answer ('informative negative for the area') is a workshop-sized result.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Promote P4 to the headline: the interesting question is not whether a location table helps (robotics says yes) but whether compiling it from 1,465 trajectories beats what a 32B model already believes, and the pre-registered top-1 row agreement covariate makes that a real study; state the paper's contribution as the compiled-vs-parametric-vs-retrieved triangle so a null on any leg is still a result. (2) Test 'retrieval cannot aggregate' against a retriever that could: add an object-conditioned retrieval arm (retrieve the k trajectories containing the goal's object class, rather than by goal sentence, which on six templates returns same-type trajectories) and a fresh k=7/k=15 arm at 8 seeds; if a k=7 object-keyed retriever recovers the same gain, the structural claim is wrong and the paper is about token cost, not about what retrieval can carry. (3) Repair the three entailment defects the automated check names: score P3 at M1 plus the measured shuffled_all - k0 gap (or as an equivalence-to-k0 test), make the both-arms-take restricted version of P7 primary or score it within the succeeded-in-both stratum, and set P8's band from paired same-arm re-run noise (~+-6) with one k3-k0 branch that actually stops the run. (4) Manipulate the search-bound property instead of naming it, as the round's binding rule demands: build a variant bank/task set in which a subset of object classes is given a deliberately flat or scene-specific placement distribution, so 'the statistic helps only where search is the bottleneck and the prior is concentrated' becomes a two-level manipulation on one environment rather than a 2-seed exploratory contrast.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, both cheap. (i) Object-conditioned retrieval: every retrieval arm here is keyed on the goal sentence (k3, k7), which on a six-template benchmark returns same-type trajectories and therefore almost never carries multiple observed placements of the target object; a retriever keyed on the object class named in the goal would put 3-7 real placements of that exact object in context and is the fair opponent for the claim that per-query retrieval 'structurally cannot' aggregate. Without it the finding is about one retriever, not about retrieval. (ii) A marginal-only receptacle-frequency list — the top receptacles overall with no object conditioning, token-matched — to separate 'the agent needs the conditional distribution P(receptacle | object)' from 'the agent just needs a good default search order'. shuffled_all is a wrong-content placebo, not a base-rate control, and on ALFWorld a bare 'check countertop, drawer, cabinet, fridge first' instruction could plausibly capture most of a +10 effect; if it does, the cross-episode-aggregate framing loses its point.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. My queries, all answered by the literature command (S2+HF); WebSearch is unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so no query used channel (b). (1) 'compiled cross-episode statistics versus retrieved trajectories agent memory' --recent: 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2606.19911 Multi-Agent Transactive Memory, 2606.05684 AdaMEM, 2605.18421 EvoMemBench, 2605.12978, 2605.12493 LongMemEval-V2 — none compiles a cross-episode statistic and compares it with retrieval at matched tokens. (2) 'object receptacle location frequency table in-context prompt LLM agent ALFWorld search': 2608.02508 RoMeRL (reduces trajectory-indexed memory utilities to fixed-dimensional per-task states — the nearest thing to 'aggregate rather than retrieve', but an RL utility state, not a location statistic, and no matched-token retrieval contrast), 2605.05413, 2605.16986, 2505.00234. (3) closest named method, 'Dynamic Cheatsheet test-time learning persistent memory reusable strategies': confirms 2504.07952, plus 2509.04439 ArcMemo, 2512.10696 ReMe, 2606.05684. (4) 'aggregating experience into a compact prior beats retrieving individual episodes embodied agent' --recent: 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2606.22844 RaMem, 2606.03951 Demo2Tutorial, 2604.05533 Echo — none. (5) home vocabulary, no agent/memory/retrieval words, 'semantic placement priors where objects are usually found guide household object search': 2607.00022 PerSim, 2606.15476 FARM, 2503.04496, 2302.12915 S^4, 2207.10761 TIDEE, 2108.00159. (6) 'can long-context LLM aggregate statistics across many in-context demonstrations explicit summary table': 2411.07130 ManyICLBench (similar-sample vs all-sample ICL — the closest existing framing of P6, on classification rather than trajectories). (7) 'static compiled playbook versus per-query retrieval matched token budget prompt caching agent benchmark' --recent: 2608.14943 Skill Blocks (caching-correct comparison of pre-load vs on-demand skill loading) — cost side only. IDs verified with s2cli paper and resolving as the proposal describes: 2504.07952, 2605.24117 SkillEvolBench, 2607.00022, 2603.05642, 2511.07800, 2512.23760, 2406.14596 ICAL; 2606.03951 Demo2Tutorial confirmed via a search hit. NOT verified: the 'WCCIS 2026' paper the proposal names as its nearest overlap — it has no arXiv id and a title query returned nothing on either channel, so the submission's central reassurance ('the nearest overlap motivates rather than tests the claim') cannot be checked by a reviewer; also unverified are 2602.06459 UcON, 2606.05684 and 2511.20857 (cited only in passing). Judging the check itself: it is better than most in this round — three query classes, IDs reported, a genuine home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words, and an honest empty result reported as empty. Two weaknesses. Its queries are uniformly placement- or cheatsheet-flavored and therefore miss the compiled-vs-raw memory literature that is the real competitor for its framing: 2605.12978 ('preserving raw episodic trajectories maintains better accuracy' than LLM-consolidated memory) and 2605.18421 EvoMemBench ('long-context baselines continue to outperform specialized memory methods') both bear directly on the Related Work assertion that whole-bank and compiled controls are not run, and the second partially pre-empts the brief's G3/G12/G17 gap. And the check's 'no pre-emption' verdict is scored on the narrow compiled-statistic-vs-retrieval comparison, which is indeed unrun, while acknowledging that the underlying mechanism is established in robotics and then treating that as confirmation; a skeptical AC reads the same fact as a novelty cost, which is where I have scored it.
